points.what: LATAM orders fell 17.0% WoW and was the largest negative contributor to the week's order change (contribution -19).
points.so_what: LATAM was the main driver pulling weekly orders down, offsetting gains from other regions.

points.what: North America orders rose 17.3% WoW, the largest positive contributor to the week's order change (contribution +24).
points.so_what: Without this gain, the weekly orders decline would have been larger.

points.what: Facebook orders fell 25.0% WoW, the largest negative contributor among traffic sources (contribution -11).
points.so_what: This pulled down overall order growth this week alongside the declines in APAC and LATAM regions.

points.what: AOV rose 7.9% WoW to $95.46, a notable move outside its usual 8-week range, and was up 4.7% YoY.
points.so_what: Revenue growth this week came from bigger order values rather than more orders, since orders fell 0.3% WoW.

points.what: Cancellation rate increased 0.9pp WoW and 1.4pp YoY, moving in the bad direction on both comparisons.
points.so_what: Bad direction on both bases confirms order quality is deteriorating, consistent with the third straight weekly increase already flagged as a risk.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of 22 Dec 2025 was 9.0%, down 1.9pp WoW and down 1.1pp YoY.
points.so_what: This is a favorable order-quality signal that moved in the opposite direction from cancellations this week.

points.what: New signups fell 6.0% WoW and 6.4% YoY to 235.
points.so_what: Signups was the only KPI moving in the wrong direction on both bases this week, a weak spot in customer growth even as orders and revenue grew year on year.

summary.headline: Orders and revenue both finished behind target this week (87.7% and 98.0%), and the year-to-date is behind too, with cancellations rising for a third straight week.

points.what: Orders were 87.7% of target and revenue was 98.0% of target this week, both behind.
points.so_what: The quarter (98.6% QTD) and year (98.6% YTD) are also running behind target, so the shortfall is not limited to this week alone.

points.what: Revenue rose 6.5% WoW to a level outside its usual 8-week range, driven by AOV up 7.9% WoW while orders fell 0.3% WoW.
points.so_what: Revenue growth this week came from bigger order values rather than more orders, and the notable revenue level should be read against still coming in behind target.

points.what: Cancellation rate rose to 15.8%, its third consecutive weekly increase from 12.5%.
points.so_what: This is a risk to revenue that is not reversing week over week, even as orders and revenue grew year on year.

points.what: New signups fell 6.0% WoW and 6.4% YoY to 235.
points.so_what: Signups is the only KPI declining on both bases this week, a risk to customer growth in an otherwise YoY-growing week.

points.what: Orders were 87.7% of target and revenue was 98.0% of target this week, both behind.
points.so_what: Both metrics grew YoY (orders 55.0%, revenue 59.7%) but not as fast as the 75% growth assumed in targets, which explains the shortfall despite growth.

points.what: QTD and YTD revenue are both 98.6% of target, a gap of $1,590 versus the target to date.
points.so_what: The quarter and year are both running behind target, matching the shortfall seen this week.

points.what: The current 8-week revenue run-rate is $50,745 per week versus the $74,080 per week required for the rest of the year, against a full-year target of $3,888,802.
points.so_what: At the recent pace, the full-year target is out of reach unless the weekly run-rate increases substantially.

points.what: Cancellation rate has risen for three consecutive weeks, from 12.5% to 15.8%.
points.so_what: Each additional percentage point of cancellations equals $678 in revenue, so a continued rise is a direct drag on revenue if it doesn't reverse.

points.what: The current 8-week revenue run-rate is $50,745 per week, well below the $74,080 per week required for the rest of the year to hit the full-year target.
points.so_what: At the current pace, the full-year revenue target is out of reach without a meaningfully faster run-rate.
